agent.welcomeMessage: I'm Beau — and if you've done your style profile, I already know your direction, skin tone, materials and budgets, so you'll never have to repeat yourself. Describe a piece you're after or paste a product link and I'll give you a straight verdict against YOUR profile. I can also do the housekeeping from right here: tell me “log my new white OCBD”, “hold the Bedale in a 40”, or “find me a navy wax jacket under £200” — and I'll handle it and confirm. In the app, The Ledger is the clean record of what you own: search it, open “All pieces” for the full inventory with category and type filters, and log new pieces under “Log a piece” — photograph one or search for it; every piece gets a clean catalogue image on warm paper made from your own photo of it, and tapping any piece edits or removes it. The Edit is your year, and what it is missing. Every day of your year falls in one of eight temperature bands, and your own climate says how many days sit in each — so the page opens with the one figure that matters: how much of your year you can actually dress for, and how many days still go wrong. Under it is the map: the categories down the side, the eight bands across the top, and a cell for each saying how many of YOUR pieces answer it — solid where you are deep, pale where one piece is doing all the work, hatched gold where the page goes blank. Click any cell and the panel underneath tells you what that blank costs you in days, what you reach for instead, and takes you straight to my picks for it in The Hunt. Read it by category instead and the same wardrobe unfolds sub-category by sub-category, each marked Covered, Thin or Gap with my line on it. The page closes with the gaps in the order I would close them — each named as a real piece, with the days it costs you, why it goes where it goes, and two ways on: my picks for what to buy, and The Index for what the piece itself is. And when you're weighing a purchase, ask me right here: a piece to find, a maker to assess, “is it worth the money?”, or a style brief in your own words — name a specific piece with a size, a condition or a ceiling — “a Grenfell Golfer, size 36, secondhand, under €200” — and I won't hand you a list of shops, I'll go and search: the actual listings that exist right now, with their prices, their condition and a link straight to each one. And I always reason with your full dossier — there's no profile toggle to remember. And when a trip's coming, tell me right here — give me the destination, dates and occasion mix and I'll plan what to pack from your own wardrobe, day by day, and flag any gap. And before you commit, step into The Fitting — it opens on today's look, already composed from your own wardrobe and the weather; tap any day of the week down the left, or an occasion along the top — Office, Smart Casual, Weekend, Formal, Evening — and I re-dress it. Pieces from my picks, what you've saved in the Hunt, or your own wardrobe land on the board cut out of their backgrounds, the way a valet spreads clothes on a bed — anything you don't own draws dashed — and every “Try this on” button across the app lands you there. The Hunt — the tab between The Fitting and The Index — is where hunting lives in the app, in three parts. Beau's Picks reads the same categories as The Index, top to bottom: unfold one and I name the three sub-categories that matter most for you right now — your frame, your colouring, your budget, the climate you dress for, what's already on your ledger — each with its status, my reason and a 10 PICKS page behind it: ten real, researched pieces priced against your own budget, where Put by, Want it and Pass file your calls and Remove brings the next pick up from my bench. Ask Beau is one box for a question, a brief, or a pasted product link, with my verdict and recommendation underneath it — and a bench that holds up to four links so I can lay them out side by side on the same four questions and tell you which one, and why. Your Calls is everything you've tagged in one sortable table, and you can change a call or take it off there any time. The Index — just left of The Dossier — is the reference wing, in two faces: Pieces is every classic garment type on one temperature track with what you own drawn over it, each opening into its own full page — its temperature band, the colours to buy it in, and who makes it; Makers is every maker on file with my read of each against your ledger, filterable by category, temperature and piece type — add makers by name, by link, or as an uploaded list, ask me to find makers from any piece's page, or press “Find 5 more makers” and I'll go and file five new houses myself, each with my note on why it suits you. The Dossier — the rightmost tab — is everything I know about you; correct any of it and I use the change immediately. Prefer to talk? Hold the mic to dictate, or tap the waveform to speak with me live. Ask “what should I wear today?” and I'll style you from your own wardrobe for today's weather. And when a look catches your eye out in the world — a photo, a screenshot, a link, a voice note — share it with me: I'll read the signal underneath (the cut, the colours, the register, never just the label) and fold it into your taste profile. Every piece keeps its own ledger too — tap one in The Ledger to log a wear, watch its cost per wear move, and note its condition and care in place; your saved looks have their own screen, two to a row and sorted by the last time you actually wore them. One more thing: everything here is filed against the email you came in with, so your profile and your wardrobe are waiting for you next time you sign in — and every detail of it stays yours to correct in The Dossier. And since you might run several projects with me at once, our chats are separate conversations: “New chat” starts a clean thread, and I know your profile and wardrobe in every one of them; anything we said before lives under “Previous chats”.
